- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or spikes too early; increase forecast slightly or smooth downward trend.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > 5x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 2x recent peak or apply decay factor.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply lagged sentiment correction (e.g., 2–3 day moving average of sentiment).
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit short-term volatility; apply mean reversion to 14-day moving average for smoothing.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), model often underperforms; use sentiment as weight to adjust forecast toward historical mean.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.33” values, model tends to underestimate; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast to compensate for pessimism.
